svg.title: PPFT features lifted to point-aligned polar tokens in PTv3
svg.desc: Dense RGB-D and polar fused PPFT features are sampled at saved point pixel coordinates to initialize one polar token per point. Shared serialization and padding produce local point and polar patches with identical support. Full joint attention mixes global action tokens with local polar and point tokens. Point and polar outputs are both inverse scattered to point indices; only action outputs are averaged across patches. Point and polar stage pooling share cluster IDs and unpool inverses.

text.tspan: PPFT + PTv3: polar patches aligned to point patches
Proposed architecture · one polar feature per point · exact shared 3D patch support
1 Lift PPFT image features to point-indexed polar tokens
Sample each scale at pixel (u_i, v_i)
Carry point_pixel_indices through filtering and point sampling.
Pixel coordinates must follow the same image transforms, camera crop and point filtering used by the model.
2 Every PTv3 block gathers matching local P / Z patches
ONE shared patch index set Ij
P ↔ A · A ↔ Z · Z ↔ P
Only A is averaged; Z stays point-indexed.
Point geometry only: CPE / spatial serialization operate on P; Z follows exactly the same indices.
Per-stream residual / normalization / FFN updates follow attention.
Optional language cross-attention: Q = P, A, Z; K/V = language context (read-only here).
Next block may change serialization order: gather both P and Z again from their point-indexed states.
Pool P and Z with the SAME cluster IDs.
Unpool with the SAME inverse map.
Use separate feature projections for P and Z.
Project A channels; keep global action tokens.
Final P + final A → action head
Z affects P and A through joint attention.
No separate polar prediction head required.
About 4× attention pairs vs. 1026-token P + A baseline.
Optional M = 16 / 32 local polar compression must
write back to per-point Z before the next serialization.
Exact support is defined by point indices and their source pixels. PPFT features may have a broader image receptive field.
